newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss economics minister has liver tumour removed.
newsitem.headline: Swiss economics minister has liver tumour removed.

text.p: Swiss Economics Minister Jean-Pascal Delamuraz, who made headlines by describing Jewish demands for quick compensation to Holocaust survivors as blackmail, had a liver tumour removed on Tuesday, the ministry said.
The tumour, taken out during a five-hour operation at Lausanne's University Hospital, is being examined to determine whether it is malignant or benign, a ministry spokesman said.
The tumour, on the right part of the liver, was discovered last week during a check-up. Delamuraz, 61, had recently been feeling uncomfortable and noticed a lack of appetite and nausea.
In December 1995 Delamuraz was also admitted to the Lausanne hospital when an artificial heart valve was inserted.

Delamuraz' blackmail remark, which stirred angry protests from international Jewish groups, came in an interview with Swiss newspapers in December, 1996, as he was finishing his one-year term in the rotating Swiss presidency.

He said any compensation by Switzerland to Jews, who might be entitled to money left in Swiss banks after World War Two, should await the findings of a panel investigating the country's role during the Nazi era.
Delamuraz later apologised for his remarks, saying they had been based on inaccurate information given to him.
